question: Many of the finest surviving ancient Greek bronze statues were found where?
answer: In the sea. On land, a bronze statue was a store of metal, and over the centuries almost all were melted into coins, tools and weapons. Only what sank out of reach escaped: the Riace warriors, the god from Cape Artemision, the Antikythera youth and the Marathon boy all came up from the seabed.
move: Ask what protected the survivors, not only what destroyed the rest.
ask: When I study winners or survivors, have I asked what protected them rather than what destroyed the rest?
trap: Picturing tombs, where so many other ancient treasures were kept safe.
reference: Jens M. Daehner & Kenneth Lapatin (eds), Power and Pathos: Bronze Sculpture of the Hellenistic World, J. Paul Getty Museum, 2015
